answer: A network can make voting power depend on a kernel of stake locked for a long period, with each account’s influence capped and rewards weighted by its history of useful, independently verified work. When several new identities coordinate, their shared funding and behavior create a ripple of correlated signals; the network can discount that cluster rather than treating each name as a person. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to tie up real capital and sustain costly work across time to grow a garden of trusted identities.
